pages.name: UTM Builder
pages.title: Free UTM Builder with GA4 Channel Check
pages.description: Build clean UTM links in seconds. See which GA4 channel each link lands in before you publish, catch naming mistakes, and download a QR code.
pages.intro: Add your page and campaign details. Your link builds as you type, and you can see which GA4 channel it will report under before you publish it.
faqs: What is a UTM link?

A UTM link is a normal web address with tracking tags added after a question mark. The tags (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content and utm_term) tell GA4 and other analytics tools where a visit came from, so you can compare campaigns that send people to the same page.
Which UTM parameters are required?

utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign. Without all three, GA4 reports the campaign as (not set) or files the visit in the wrong channel. utm_content and utm_term are optional and are mostly used for ad variations and keywords.
Why does my campaign traffic show as Unassigned in GA4?

GA4 sorts visits into channels using fixed rules on the source and medium. A medium it doesn't recognise, such as "paid-ads" or "influencer" from an unknown source, matches no rule and ends up in Unassigned. The channel check in this builder runs the same rules, so you can fix the link before it goes live.
What are utm_id, utm_source_platform, utm_creative_format and utm_marketing_tactic?

These are extra parameters GA4 can collect. utm_id is a campaign ID that lets you join cost data imported into GA4. The other three describe the buying platform, the creative format and the targeting tactic. They are optional and sit under Extra GA4 fields.
Is anything I type saved or sent anywhere?
No. The builder runs entirely in your browser. Your recent links are stored only in this browser so you can copy or export them later, and you can clear them at any time.
pages.content:
What UTM tags do

UTM tags are short labels added to the end of a link. When someone clicks, your analytics reads the labels and records exactly where the visit came from. No extra code is needed for GA4 to read them.

TagAnswersExample
utm_sourceWhere did the click come from?google, facebook, newsletter
utm_mediumWhat type of traffic is it?cpc, paid_social, email
utm_campaignWhich campaign was it?spring-sale_{{YYYYMM}}
utm_contentWhich ad or link was clicked?hero-banner, video-a
utm_termWhich keyword or audience?running shoes

Why UTM tags matter

  • Credit goes to the right campaign. Without tags, a click from an email or WhatsApp message often shows up as Direct, and the campaign that earned it gets no credit.
  • Channels are compared fairly. One naming convention across every channel means paid, owned and partner traffic line up in the same report.
  • Leads and revenue connect to marketing. Stored with each lead, UTM tags show which campaign produced customers, not just clicks.
  • Budget follows results. Clean data shows which ads and messages to scale and which to stop.

How to use this builder

  1. Paste the page you want people to land on. Existing UTM tags are picked up so you can edit them.
  2. Pick a channel shortcut or type your own source, medium and campaign. Values are lowercased and cleaned as you type.
  3. Check the GA4 channel and any warnings, then copy the link, open it to test, or download a QR code.

The naming convention

Pattern: {offer-or-theme}_{product-or-audience}_{market}_{yyyymm}

Example: spring-sale_running-shoes_uae_{{YYYYMM}}

Pick the parts your reports need, keep them in the same order every time, and write them down where the whole team can see them. Need a ready-made convention? The industry builders below each come with one.

Tips

  • Keep everything lowercase. GA4 treats Facebook and facebook as two different sources, so one campaign splits into two rows.
  • Never tag internal links on your own site. A UTM click starts a new session and overwrites the original source.
  • Use utm_content to tell apart ads or links that point to the same page, and utm_term for keywords or audiences.
  • Agree a separator rule: hyphens inside a value, underscores between parts of a campaign name, so names can be split back out in a spreadsheet.

Getting UTM data into your database

GA4 counts visits. Your CRM or database records who became a lead or customer. Unless the UTM tags are saved with each record, the two never meet, and you can't tell which campaign produced which sale. Share this brief with your website developer.

What to ask for

  1. Read the UTM tags and ad click IDs from the URL on every page load.
  2. Save them in a first-party cookie for 90 days. Keep a first-touch copy that is never overwritten, and a last-touch copy that updates on each new tagged visit.
  3. Ignore visits without UTM tags, so an untagged return visit never wipes the saved values.
  4. Add hidden fields for every value to every form: contact, booking, sign-up and checkout.
  5. Fill the hidden fields from the cookie when the form is sent.
  6. Store each value in its own column on the lead or order record, and map the same fields into the CRM.
  7. Test it: open a tagged link, send a form, and check the record shows the right values.

Fields to add to each lead or order

FieldWhat it holds
first_utm_source … first_utm_termFirst tagged visit. Set once, never overwritten.
last_utm_source … last_utm_termMost recent tagged visit before the form was sent.
gclid, fbclid, msclkidAd click IDs, for offline conversion uploads.
landing_pageFull URL of the first page seen.
referrerThe site the visitor came from.
first_touch_at, last_touch_atTimestamps of both visits.

A starting point for the developer

const KEYS=['utm_source','utm_medium','utm_campaign','utm_content','utm_term','gclid','fbclid','msclkid'];
const q=new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const hit={};KEYS.forEach(k=>{if(q.get(k))hit[k]=q.get(k);});
if(Object.keys(hit).length){
  hit.landing_page=location.href;hit.referrer=document.referrer;hit.at=new Date().toISOString();
  const save=(n,v)=>document.cookie=n+'='+encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify(v))+';path=/;max-age=7776000;SameSite=Lax';
  if(!document.cookie.includes('utm_first='))save('utm_first',hit);
  save('utm_last',hit);
}

pages.name: Healthcare UTM Builder
pages.title: Healthcare UTM Builder for Hospitals & Clinics
pages.description: A free UTM builder for hospitals, clinics and healthcare marketers. Name campaigns by service line, objective and language, and see the GA4 channel before you publish.
pages.h1: UTM builder for hospitals and clinics.
pages.intro: Pick a channel, choose the service line and objective, and the campaign name follows one convention every time.
faqs: Can I put a medical condition in a campaign name?

Service-line and campaign-level names such as "cardiology" or "fertility-ivf" are common and fine. What must never go in a link is anything about an individual: names, record numbers, contact details or a specific patient's condition. Check your hospital's privacy policy and local health advertising rules for anything more sensitive.
How should a hospital structure UTM campaign names?

Start with the parts you report on most. A common order is facility, service line, objective, audience, language and date, for example "main-campus_cardiology_appointments_patients_ar_202610". Underscores separate the parts, so you can split them into columns in Looker Studio or a spreadsheet.
How do I track appointments that come from Google Business Profile?

Add a UTM link to the website field of each profile, with source google, medium organic and a campaign name that starts with gbp. GA4 keeps the visit in Organic Search, and the campaign name lets you separate it from regular search results.
Why should Arabic and English campaigns be tagged separately?
Language changes audience, competition and conversion rates. Tagging language in the campaign name lets you compare cost per lead and booking rates by language without relying on ad platform labels.
Do UTMs work for phone calls and WhatsApp enquiries?

UTMs only travel with the click. To connect calls or WhatsApp chats to campaigns, use call tracking numbers that change based on the UTM source, or pass the UTMs into a pre-filled WhatsApp message or form.

pages.name: Ecommerce UTM Builder
pages.title: Ecommerce UTM Builder for Online Stores
pages.description: A free UTM builder for online stores. Tag Shopping, PMax, Meta, TikTok, email flows and influencers with one naming convention, and check the GA4 channel before launch.
pages.intro: Pick a channel, choose the campaign type and product or category, and the campaign name follows one convention every time.
faqs: Why do my Google Shopping clicks show as Paid Search in GA4?

GA4 only reports Paid Shopping when the source is a known shopping site or the campaign name contains "shop" or "shopping". Google is a search engine, so a campaign called "summer-sale" from google / cpc becomes Paid Search. Adding "shopping" to the campaign name fixes it, which is what the Shopping preset in this builder does.
Should I use UTMs and discount codes for influencers?
Use both. Codes catch buyers who type them in later, and UTMs catch people who click and buy without a code. Put the creator handle in utm_content so each creator has their own row in GA4.
Do UTMs conflict with Meta's fbclid or Google's gclid?
No. Click IDs are added automatically by the platforms and work alongside your UTMs. Just don't paste a click ID into a link you are building, because it belongs to one specific click.
How do I tag email flows such as abandoned cart?

Use medium email, a dedicated source such as "automation", and a campaign name that describes the flow, for example "abandoned-cart_all-products_uae". Many email platforms can add UTMs automatically; match their settings to the same convention.
What should I use for marketplace links such as Amazon?
Links from your marketplace store to your own site can use source amazon and medium referral. GA4 recognises Amazon as a shopping site and reports it as Organic Shopping.

Why do my Google Shopping clicks show as Paid Search in GA4?

GA4 only reports Paid Shopping when the source is a known shopping site or the campaign name contains "shop" or "shopping". Should I use UTMs and discount codes for influencers?

pages.content:
What UTM tags do

UTM tags are short labels added to the end of a link. When someone clicks, your analytics reads the labels and records exactly where the visit came from. No extra code is needed for GA4 to read them.

TagAnswersExample
utm_sourceWhere did the click come from?google, facebook, newsletter
utm_mediumWhat type of traffic is it?cpc, paid_social, email
utm_campaignWhich campaign was it?spring-sale_{{YYYYMM}}
utm_contentWhich ad or link was clicked?hero-banner, video-a
utm_termWhich keyword or audience?running shoes

Why UTM tags matter

  • Credit goes to the right campaign. Without tags, a click from an email or WhatsApp message often shows up as Direct, and the campaign that earned it gets no credit.
  • Channels are compared fairly. One naming convention across every channel means paid, owned and partner traffic line up in the same report.
  • Leads and revenue connect to marketing. Stored with each lead, UTM tags show which campaign produced customers, not just clicks.
  • Budget follows results. Clean data shows which ads and messages to scale and which to stop.

How to use this builder

  1. Paste the landing page, gated asset page or demo page.
  2. Choose the channel, including review sites, partners, events and sales outreach.
  3. Build the campaign name from product, offer type, funnel stage, segment, region and date.
  4. Copy the link, and make sure your forms pass the UTMs into the CRM.

The naming convention

Pattern: {product}_{type}_{stage}_{date}

Example: analytics-suite_webinar_tofu_{{YYYYMM}}

Parts are joined with underscores and words inside a part use hyphens, so you can split the name back into columns in a spreadsheet or Looker Studio. Optional parts are skipped when empty. You can switch the separator under Formatting rules.

Tips for b2b marketers

  • Capture UTMs in hidden form fields and store them on the contact in HubSpot, Salesforce or your CRM. GA4 alone can't tell you which campaign became pipeline.
  • Keep sales outreach on its own source. It's the cleanest way to split marketing-sourced and sales-sourced pipeline.
  • Tag the funnel stage. It stops a cheap top-of-funnel ebook from being judged against a demo campaign on cost per lead.
  • Use utm_term for job title or matched audience on LinkedIn so you can see which roles convert, not just which ads.
  • Tag employee advocacy links separately from the company page. Personal profiles usually drive more clicks than brand posts.

Getting UTM data into your database

GA4 counts visits. Your CRM or database records who became a lead or customer. Unless the UTM tags are saved with each record, the two never meet, and you can't tell which campaign produced which sale. Share this brief with your website developer.

What to ask for

  1. Read the UTM tags and ad click IDs from the URL on every page load.
  2. Save them in a first-party cookie for 90 days. Keep a first-touch copy that is never overwritten, and a last-touch copy that updates on each new tagged visit.
  3. Ignore visits without UTM tags, so an untagged return visit never wipes the saved values.
  4. Add hidden fields for every value to every form: contact, booking, sign-up and checkout.
  5. Fill the hidden fields from the cookie when the form is sent.
  6. Store each value in its own column on the lead or order record, and map the same fields into the CRM.
  7. Test it: open a tagged link, send a form, and check the record shows the right values.

Fields to add to each lead or order

FieldWhat it holds
first_utm_source … first_utm_termFirst tagged visit. Set once, never overwritten.
last_utm_source … last_utm_termMost recent tagged visit before the form was sent.
gclid, fbclid, msclkidAd click IDs, for offline conversion uploads.
landing_pageFull URL of the first page seen.
referrerThe site the visitor came from.
first_touch_at, last_touch_atTimestamps of both visits.

A starting point for the developer

const KEYS=['utm_source','utm_medium','utm_campaign','utm_content','utm_term','gclid','fbclid','msclkid'];
const q=new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const hit={};KEYS.forEach(k=>{if(q.get(k))hit[k]=q.get(k);});
if(Object.keys(hit).length){
  hit.landing_page=location.href;hit.referrer=document.referrer;hit.at=new Date().toISOString();
  const save=(n,v)=>document.cookie=n+'='+encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify(v))+';path=/;max-age=7776000;SameSite=Lax';
  if(!document.cookie.includes('utm_first='))save('utm_first',hit);
  save('utm_last',hit);
}

Never put names, emails or phone numbers in UTM tags. Store them only in your own database, under your privacy policy.

Frequently asked questions

How do I get UTM data into HubSpot or Salesforce?

Add hidden fields for each UTM to your forms and fill them from the page URL, or use your CRM's built-in tracking. Store first-touch and last-touch values separately so long sales cycles keep the original source.

Should LinkedIn paid and organic posts use different UTMs?

Yes. Use medium paid_social for ads and social for company page and employee posts. GA4 then reports them as Paid Social and Organic Social, and you can compare them fairly.

How do I tag webinars?
